Monica,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement review I need formal confirmation and evidence for the following for the NovaHealth EU deployment (planned cutover Q4):

- Confirmation that all customer data for the NovaHealth account will be persistently stored only in EU-hosted regions (no automatic replication to other regions unless explicitly enabled).
- Evidence of network controls for a Private deployment: VPC peering/private-link diagram, peering/endpoint IP ranges, and whether Redwoods supports a PrivateLink (or equivalent) with our VNet/VPC.
- Can we BYOK (customer-managed KMS) in the EU region? If yes, what gating steps are required and estimated lead time?
- Retention & access: audit log retention period, ability to provide audit logs for SOC2 requests, and whether logs are stored in-region.
- Any redacted SOC2 / CAIQ / SIG items covering data residency and isolation we can share with our security team.

We also have a short SIG baseline questionnaire that we can share; if you can send the CAIQ mapping or point us to the file in a shared folder that would be helpful.

Can we schedule a 30m technical alignment next week? Prefer Aug 27 in the morning CET.

Thanks,

Thanks Sam — happy to run through this and provide the artifacts.

Quick answers up front:
- Redwood can ensure persistent customer data for the NovaHealth account is stored in EU regions only; cross-region replication is not enabled by default and requires an explicit opt-in.
- We support a PrivateLink-style endpoint for AWS and an equivalent Private Endpoint model for Azure. We can provide a VPC/VNet diagram, endpoint IP ranges, and a short checklist for connection (IP allowlist, TLS cert path, shared prefix).
- BYOK is supported in EU: customers can bring an AWS KMS key or Azure Key Vault key. There are a couple of policy checks and a secure transfer step — in short, 3–7 business days to validate and provision once we have the key ARN/identifier and account owner contact.
- Audit logs: default retention is 90 days in-region; we can extend retention up to 12 months for enterprise plans and provide S3/Blob export for longer-term retention. Logs for SOC2 evidence are provided as redacted extracts via a secure transfer.

I'll attach the SOC2 Type II summary and a CAIQ mapping workbook to this thread and open a shared Drive folder for the NovaHealth team. Laura — can you confirm which parts of the SOC2 report we can share wholesale vs redacted? Vivek/Rishi — can you attach the latest EU network design and confirm any egress constraints?

1) I’ll share attachments and a read-only Drive folder (link below).
2) Quick alignment call — I’ve proposed Aug 27 09:30 CET (calendar link below).
3) If NovaHealth wants BYOK, Sam/Procurement upload the key policy via the secure upload link and we’ll queue the integration.

Folks — quick internal note before we send to NovaHealth.

- SOC2: We can share the SOC2 Type II report summary (controls, scope, auditor opinion) and a limited set of control narratives. The full report is covered by NDA; we can provide it via our dataroom if NovaHealth signs the standard NDA (we already have an NDA template to expedite).
- CAIQ / SIG: I’ve attached the CAIQ mapping workbook (caiq-responses-novahc-2026.xlsx). It maps our controls to the SIG/CAIQ questions NovaHealth flagged (data residency, key management, isolation).
- KMS/BYOK: We support customer-managed keys. For AWS: we accept KMS key ARNs with an IAM policy that allows our service principal to use the key. For Azure: customer must provide the Key Vault resource ID and grant the Redwood service principal get/wrap/unwrap rights. We maintain key material in-region and do not export key material outside EU.
- Private connectivity: redwood_eu_network_design_v2.pdf is the requested diagram. It shows a PrivateLink endpoint in the EU region, egress NAT gateways scoped to region, and optional VPC peering. IP ranges are in the diagram appendix (page 3).
- Logs: We keep service audit logs (API access, admin actions) in-region and can provide extracts for SOC2 requests. Default 90 days; export to S3/Blob possible under an enterprise addendum.

Quick technical confirmations to include in the outgoing note to NovaHealth:

- Private connectivity model: we expose a region-scoped PrivateLink endpoint (AWS) and Private Endpoint (Azure). Connection is established from NovaHealth's VPC/VNet to the endpoint; traffic terminates in our EU-only tenant. No cross-region backplane traffic unless customer enables cross-region replication.
- Egress control: outbound connectivity from the private endpoint goes through region-scoped NAT / egress gateways. Customer-facing egress IP ranges are documented in redwood_eu_network_design_v2.pdf (appendix).
- KMS: Customer keys remain in-customer account/KeyVault/KMS. Redwood stores only a reference and uses the provider's crypto APIs; key material never leaves the configured region. Rotation policy can follow customer's schedule; we recommend a 90-day rotation cadence for high-sensitivity customers.
- Logs & retention: service audit logs retained 90 days by default in EU. We can configure push to customer-owned S3/Blob (in-region) for longer retention, or deliver on-demand extracts for compliance reviews.
- Provisioning lead time: For a Private deployment + BYOK validation we estimate 5–7 business days once the key & connectivity details are provided. If NovaHealth requires our team to perform key import/verification, add 2 business days.

I’ve added a short technical appendix in the Drive folder with example Terraform snippets and the endpoint allowlist CSV. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-novahc-eu (internal access may require the read-only token we shared).

— Vivek
VP, Infrastructure Engineering

Sam — thanks for the checklist. Per our call and internal follow-ups, please find the items we can share attached and next steps below. If you need anything redacted before wider distribution to your security team, let us know and Laura will provide a sanitized copy.

Summary answers:
- Data locality: Customer data for the NovaHealth account will reside only in the EU region instance (we use eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 depending on your preference). Cross-region replication is off by default and requires an explicit configuration change by NovaHealth.
- Private connectivity: We support PrivateLink (AWS) and Private Endpoint (Azure) and will provide the endpoint DNS and IPs. Connection checklist attached (see network design PDF).
- BYOK: Supported. Please use the secure upload link to provide the key identifier and policy: https://secureupload.redwood.example.com/upload/NH-keys. Required items: key ARN / Key Vault ID, owner contact, and the policy statements granting Redwood use (get, decrypt, wrapKey/unwrapKey as applicable). Estimated validation 3–7 business days.
- Logs & retention: Default 90 days, can push to your S3/Blob in EU for longer retention. Audit extracts for SOC2 reviews provided via secure transfer.
